entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT PATNA
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

This application, for grant of anticipatory bail, arises out of Mirganj Police Station Case No. 31 of 2016, disclosing offences under Sections 272, 273, 420, 120B of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 26 (i) (iv)/31 of the Food Adulteration Act and Section 6 (A) (B) of the COTPA Act.
Allegedly, a pick-up van, carrying total 16 bags, containing 6000 packets, marked with M branded chewing tobacco and 240 bags, containing 12000 packets of Madhu was recovered.
The driver is said to have disclosed the name of the petitioner from whose godown the said articles were loaded.

Learned Senior Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has submitted that his implication is based on the disclosure made by the driver of the said pick up van and there is no other material against the petitioner beyond that.
He has further submitted that even if the allegations are treated to be true, no offence under Sections 272 or 273 of the Indian Penal Code is made out.

According to him, strictly speaking, the petitioner cannot be prosecuted under the provisions of the Food and Adulteration Act, in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court, in the case of M/s Omkar Ajay Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Bihar on 4 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161525157/
1

entities.text: Agency and Others v. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and Others, reported in 2016 (3) PLJR 667
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the above submission, this application is allowed.

Let the petitioner, Ajay Kumar Gupta, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the Court below within six weeks, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Purnea,
in connection with Mirganj Police Station Case No. 31 of 2016, subject to the condition laid down under Section 438 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

This is subject to the condition that the petitioner shall present himself before the police/Court, as the case may be, as and when required and in the event of failure on his part to appear before the Court on two consecutive occasions, his bail bond shall be liable to be cancelled.

(Chakradhari Sharan Singh, 
Prabhakar Anand/-c  U  T  Ajay Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Bihar on 4 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161525157/
2
